title: Labour-Market Softening Cements Rate-Cut Bets Ahead of Jackson Hole, Pressuring Dollar and Yields
content: The window's dominant story was the collapse of hike risk into rate-cut conviction. The Fed held at 3.50-3.75% in late July with three officials dissenting in favour of a hike, keeping the dollar bid, before the 1 August payrolls report broke that framing as employment fell and prior months were revised sharply lower. A cool July CPI, headline near 3.3% and core around 2.5%, reinforced the disinflation, lifting September cut odds and dragging the dollar to a three-month low and front-end yields lower. Attention converged on Jackson Hole on 27-29 August and Chair Warsh's first keynote for confirmation of an easing bias ahead of the 16 September FOMC. The repricing rippled across assets, supporting equities and precious metals, and left every subsequent jobs and inflation print pivotal for cross-asset direction.

title: Long-End Fiscal Strain Drives Bear-Steepening as US Debt Tops $40tn and Treasury Ramps Buybacks
content: A distinct, reinforcing theme was mounting strain at the long end of the curve even as the front end rallied on cut bets. Longer yields climbed through the window, the 30-year pressing towards 5.25% and the 10-year near 4.7%, producing pronounced bear-steepening as investors demanded a higher term premium. The pressure reflected heavy deficit spending, swelling AI-related corporate issuance and the national debt crossing $40tn in mid-August. Treasury responded on 19 August by at least doubling its long-dated buybacks from September, briefly easing yields; the relief quickly reversed, underscoring scepticism that the operation could offset structural supply. The episode kept fiscal sustainability and bond-market functioning central to the macro debate, weighed on the dollar and reinforced steepening as a favoured cross-asset expression tied to duration, deficits and Treasury supply dynamics.

title: Gold and Silver Extend Record Run as Debasement Hedge Amid Softer Dollar and Fiscal Angst
content: Precious metals' structural bull run persisted as the window's clearest cross-asset hedge signal, with bullion climbing to roughly a three-month high near $4,600 and silver pushing past $69. The advance drew on the same forces unsettling bonds and the currency: a dollar sliding to a three-month low, the dovish rate repricing, ballooning deficits and debt crossing $40tn, and questions over policy credibility under a new Fed chair. Treasury's buyback intervention and steepening long-end yields amplified the debasement narrative rather than dampening it. Notably, metals rallied alongside near-record equities and a weaker dollar, signalling investors were hedging currency and fiscal risk rather than pricing recession. The move cemented precious metals' role as the market's preferred store of value, leaving them sensitive to the dollar, real yields and the evolving Jackson Hole policy signal.
